summary: Page-level title chrome with route identity, responsive ordered button, icon, menu, split, and overflow actions, plus explicit expanded, compact, or constrained variants.
useWhen: A top-level page needs one h1 above its content.
A list or detail page has multiple route-level sections that belong in the inline active-section menu.
A detail page needs route ancestors in expanded presentation and a page-level Back action in compact chrome.
A page needs an ordered set of primary, secondary, icon, menu, split, or overflow commands.
avoidWhen: The title belongs to a PanelTools drawer or fullscreen pane; use PanelToolHeader through PanelTools instead.
The choices are primary application destinations or BarNav destinations rather than sections within the current page.
The heading belongs to a card, modal, or other bounded region rather than the page.
Local panels inside page content should remain directly selectable; use TabGroup instead.
Automatic sticky or responsive page orchestration is required; compose BarTitle in ShellPage rather than implementing it in the header.

alternatives.when: A create or edit workflow needs Exit, persistent step navigation, and a final Save or Submit action.
alternatives.reason: BarWorkflow owns compact-only workflow progression rather than responsive page identity.

alternatives.when: The header belongs to a PanelTools product view.
alternatives.reason: PanelToolHeader owns pane-level Back and actions without creating page chrome.

alternatives.when: A small set of inner-page panels should remain visible as tabs.
alternatives.reason: TabGroup is the local content-view control rather than route-level page title chrome.

accessibility: Provide one concise heading; BarTitle renders exactly one h1 and changes only its visual recipe between variants.
Give compact Back a destination-specific accessible name such as Back to Drivers and handle dsBack in the route owner.
Provide ordered breadcrumb items for deeper expanded paths and handle dsBreadcrumbSelect when native href navigation is not used; backLabel remains the single-parent expanded fallback.
Keep value synchronized with the current child route; dsSectionChange returns the selected section id.
Section and overflow triggers expose menu relationships and restore focus after selection or dismissal.
Use one filled primary action in the page decision area, give icon and menu triggers specific accessible names, and mark destructive overflow actions explicitly.
Keep every top-level action and nested menu-choice id non-empty and unique; dsAction emits the selected id without adding a parent prefix.
states: Omitting Back, sections, primaryAction, and actions produces the top-level title-only header.
Two or more selectable sections add the inline section trigger; one section does not render a redundant menu.
Dividers in sections or actions create separate Menu groups without becoming selectable rows.
The overflow trigger uses its bordered treatment whenever any visible action sits beside it; overflow-only presentations keep the trigger borderless.

Ordered actions preserve authored order, but only the first eligible filled button, unfilled button, icon button, labeled menu button, or split button renders beside the title. Remaining commands use the shared overflow, whose rows are text-only. Menu choices and overflowed split commands become separate rows and share the same flat action event.

expanded renders the larger heading, optional description, inset divider, and a full-width caption breadcrumb row above the title. The breadcrumb begins after 32px top padding; the following title and right-side actions share one top alignment. Compact renders 48px chrome with the existing icon Back action; constrained uses compact chrome and moves an auto-collapse primary action into overflow.

The one visible ordered action collapses by default in constrained presentation. Use never for an exceptional action whose hierarchy must remain visible; explicit overflow actions never leave the shared menu.

showDivider=false removes the bottom divider when the surrounding page composition supplies the boundary; showCompactDivider can independently restore or remove that boundary in compact and constrained variants.

placement=shell-bar is reserved for ShellApp panel section navigation. It remains compact, omits description and breadcrumb presentation, and preserves applicable Back, section, primary, and overflow controls.

Section, action, split-menu, and overflow triggers automatically retain the shared surface-open wash through exit. The expanded header presentation is layout, not surface ownership, and does not itself acquire a pressed wash.
responsiveBehavior: BarTitle does not observe viewport, shell, scroll, or container state. Its owner selects an explicit variant.
ShellPage is the standard owner for automatic expanded, compact, and constrained selection.
ShellApp owns shell-bar placement and always selects compact presentation there; mobile continues to use MobileHeader.
When ShellPage owns BarTitle on a secondary desktop or tablet page, its expanded, compact, and constrained presentations all match that canvas; the separate MobileHeader component remains primary.

Compact titles use the shared compact-header geometry and md control inset so top-level headings align with BarNav and inline Back geometry aligns with PanelToolHeader. Long headings and section labels truncate independently while Back and action controls retain complete hit targets and accessible names.
A never-collapse action remains visible in constrained mode; the title and section label yield space first.
On mobile, icon commands remain visible by default while labeled buttons, labeled menus, split buttons, and explicit overflow commands become one flat overflow menu derived by ShellApp.

customElements: Assign breadcrumbs, sections, actionItems, primaryAction, and actions as JavaScript properties and replace array or object identities when controlled state changes.
Handle dsBack for compact navigation and dsBreadcrumbSelect for application-owned expanded breadcrumb navigation, update value after dsSectionChange, and execute product commands from dsAction.
react: Pass breadcrumb, section, and ordered action arrays directly to DsBarTitle and keep value controlled from route state.
Place DsBarTitle in DsShellPage with slot=header when automatic page behavior is required.
angular: Bind complex values on the standalone DsBarTitle adapter and handle Back, breadcrumb, section, and action intent events in the route shell.
Place ds-bar-title in ds-shell-page with slot=header; do not render router-outlet inside BarTitle.
